title: Level 5 (World Class) - A-17
notes:
West leads the ♣6 against 6♠. East likely has the ♥K and ♦A for his 2 level overcall. South must plan to squeeze East in hearts and clubs. If South takes dummy's ♣K in order to finesse in spades, he will go down even if East has the ♠Q. South draws the rest of the trump.

In order to squeeze East, South will have to set up and cash a diamond trick first. After winning the ♦A East will return a club, putting South back in his hand. South can only get to the ♦K in hearts and playing hearts will destroy the entry for the squeeze. No 3 suit squeeze is possible if South runs spades without giving up a diamond trick.

South cannot afford to take the percentage play in spades. He must hope for one of the defenders to have a doubleton ♠Q. South should win the ♣A and cash the ♠A and ♠K. When the ♠Q drops, South draws the last trump. South must take care to keep at least 3 diamonds in dummy.

South next leads the ♦Q which East must win (or South could play on hearts). South wins East's diamond or club return in dummy and cashes dummy's other minor suit King making sure to pitch a heart on the ♦K.

South ruffs a diamond back to his hand and finishes the trumps. When South leads the last trump East has no answer. There is no ambiguity, South merely has to count clubs.
